analyst_reports.business_description: Twenty-year-old data-integration and analytics software vendor. ~55% of revenue from government / defense / intelligence agencies on multi-year contracts with very high switching costs and security-accreditation moats; the rest is commercial enterprise. Software is deployed against the customer's own sensitive data (ontology / pipeline layer), sold top-down, and usage expands within accounts over years. Founder-led, dual-class shares, famously mission-driven/contrarian culture. Heavy stock-based compensation is the main shareholder complaint.
recent_developments: Second consecutive GAAP-profitable quarter just reported, including the FIRST quarter of positive GAAP operating income; management raised the profitability outlook and now commits to GAAP net income in EVERY quarter of the fiscal year.

A few weeks BEFORE the print, the company announced a new product layer that puts large-language-model interfaces on top of its existing data platform, targeting rapid enterprise adoption of generative AI on private data. Management calls the depth of engagement and demand 'without precedent'; no revenue from it has been disclosed yet.
US commercial customer count grew 50% YoY (103 -> 155); quarterly adjusted free cash flow hit a record 36% margin on better collections and cost discipline.
Growth is still only ~18% YoY — the long eight-quarter deceleration has flattened rather than re-accelerated, and the full-year revenue guide implies ~15-17% growth.

Bear case: the stock has nearly doubled in a month on the print plus AI enthusiasm and now trades ~16x trailing sales vs de-rated peers at ~6-12x; skeptics argue the new AI layer is a repackaging of the existing platform with no proven monetization, and SBC still runs near 30% of revenue.
Government business remains the anchor (latest quarter +20% YoY) with defense budgets in its home market rising.
analyst_reports.macro_context: After the fastest central-bank tightening cycle in decades and a 60-80% de-rating of unprofitable software, rates have plateaued; investor enthusiasm for perceived beneficiaries of a new wave of generative-AI adoption has sharply re-rated a handful of names in recent weeks.
